title.narrative: New phase of support to SCTM
Ny fas av stöd till SCTM

description.narrative: By 2020 Serbian municipalities will be better prepared for EU accession with improved service delivery, enhanced dialogue with stakeholders and more efficient and transparent local administrations, in accordance with the principles of good governance and gender equality. Note: The project was extended in December 2020 (cost extension). The new end date for the activity period is December 31, 2021.

Standing Conference of Towns and Municipalities (SCTM) i Serbien och Sveriges Kommuner och Landsting (SKL) lade fram ett förslag till ett program med titeln: "Support to Serbian Municipalities on the Road to EU Accession: Enabling High-Quality Services, Stakeholder Dialogue and Efficient Local Administration", i september 2015. Sidas första bedömning, inklusive diskussion på QAC, var att ytterligare samråd behövs med SCTM och SKL för att slutföra förslaget i linje med Sidas kommentarer och krav. Slutliga versionen av förslaget (inklusive budget och RBM) lämnades in den 22 december 2015.
Det föreslagna programmet är en fyraårig insats (2016 - 2020) för att stödja serbiska kommuner med det övergripande målet att förbereda dem inför EU-anslutningen, med förbättrade förutsättningar för tjänster med hög kvalitet, förstärkt dialog med intressenter och effektivare lokala förvaltningar, i enlighet med principerna om god förvaltning och jämställdhet. Insatsen kommer att genomföras i samarbete mellan serbiska och svenska lokala myndigheter, SCTM och SKL, och är en fortsättning på det framgångsrika projekt som genomfördes mellan 2011 och 2015. Med utgångspunkt i erfarenheterna från den tidigare fasen, kommer den nya insatsen införa kommunala stödpaket (Municipal Support packages - MSPs) med målet att hjälpa kommuner att göra konkreta framsteg inom tre tematiska områden: miljöskydd och tjänster, förbättring av affärsklimatet på lokal nivå och förbättra förebyggande och hantering av nödsituationer. Den andra komponenten av programmet ska vidareutveckla SCTM:s kapacitet att se till att kommunala intressen beaktas på nationell nivå. Denna komponent kommer att behandla följande områden: 1) miljöskydd, 2) förbättring av affärsklimatet på lokal nivå, 3) EU-integration och internationellt samarbete, 4) jämställdhet, 5) förbättrat förebyggande och hantering av nödsituationer på lokal nivå och 6) kapacitetsutveckling och hållbarhet av SCTM.
Den totala kostnaden för projektet uppgår till 32 233 671. Av detta belopp kommer 16 672 725 att göras tillgängliga för SKL (i enlighet med SKL budget) och 15 560 946 kommer att göras tillgängliga för SCTM för genomförande av verksamhet i Serbien (i enlighet med SCTM budget). Sida åtar sig att finansiera högst SEK 32 233 671.
Insatsen "Support to Serbian Municipalities on the Road to EU Accession: Enabling Hugh-Quality Services, Stakeholder Dialogue and Efficient Local Administration" är nu under det andra året för genomförandet. Sammantaget går projektet framåt och i linje med planerna som föreslås i förslaget. Detta bekräftades vid det årliga översynsmötet som ägde rum i mars 2017 och i efterföljande uppföljningsmöten som Sida hade med både SCTM och SALAR.
Denna fas av stöd till lokal styrning i Serbien, genom partnerskap mellan SCTM och SALAR för första gången, förutsätter också att man stöder utvalda kommuner direkt via kommunala supportpaket (MSP) på följande tematiska områden: 1) Miljöskydd och tjänster, 2) förbättring av affärsklimatet och 3) förbättrad förebyggande och hantering av nödsituationer. Eftersom detta sätt att stödja LSG är ganska innovativt, och med tanke på att deras (LSG) behov är stora med avseende på kapacitetsuppbyggnad och andra former av stöd var intresset på LSG: s sida ovanligt högt. Alla ansökningar från kommuner kunde emellertid inte godtas på grund av programmets ekonomiska begränsningar.
Med utgångspunkt från mycket höga intressen bland kommuner för att få stöd via MSP, liksom relevansen av tematiska områden som omfattas av dessa anläggningar för kommuner, Serbiens integrationsprocess, men även genomförandet av Sveriges resultatstrategi för Västra Balkan och Turkiet i Serbien, har SCTM och SALAR utvecklat ett förslag och bad Sida att tillhandahålla ytterligare medel till programmet, så att antalet kommuner som fick stöd kunde ökas.
Med detta förslag skulle programmets totala budget ökas från 32 233 671 till 42 311 027; ytterligare 3 669 856 kronor ska fördelas och utbetalas till SALAR och 6 407 500 kronor till SCTM.

The proposed program is a four-year intervention to support Serbian LSGs with the overall aim of preparing them for EU accession, with improved conditions for high quality services, enhanced dialogue with stakeholders and more efficient local administrations, in accordance with the principles of good governance and gender equality. The intervention will be implemented in partnership between the Serbian and Swedish local government associations, SCTM and SALAR, continuing the successful approach implemented between 2011 and 2015. Building on experiences from the previous phase, the new intervention will introduce Municipal Support Packages (MSPs) with the aim to help concrete municipalities make concrete progress within three thematic areas: environmental protection and services, improvement of business climate at local level and improved prevention and management of emergency situations. The second program component would further develop SCTM’s capacities to ensure that local government interests are taken into account at national level. This Component will deal with the following thematic areas: 1) environmental protection, 2) improvement of business climate at local level, 3) EU integration and international cooperation, 4) gender equality, 5) improved prevention and management of emergency situations at local level and 6) capacity development and sustainability of SCTM.

sector.narrative: Decentralisation and support to subnational government

description.narrative:
The project was launched in April 2016, and finalized in April 2022.
At the start of the project, SCTM identified several challenges within the environmental area. In summary, deficiencies in environmental law enforcement at the local level were identified as a consequence of inadequately organized and understaffed environmental administrative structures. By the time of the project finalization, the LSGs have gone from a reactive to a proactive approach. All targeted LSGs succeeded in improving management of the Public Utility Companies (PUC) and the local administration with regards to service delivery in sectors of water and sanitation and waste management based on community needs and available resources. Through the work with MSPs, two main results came as a positive fallout for all LSGs. First, the Methodology and Guide on customer satisfaction on communal services, was developed (based on the obligation from article 13 in the Law on Communal Services). The methodology was formulated thanks to work developed through MSP Zrenjanin with the aim to increase the interaction between the LSGs, the PUCs and the citizens in order to improve PUC management and delivery of services. Citizens satisfaction survey on the delivery of PUC services was used as the starting point. This methodology is now used by other LSGs as a tool in all cases when customer satisfaction on communal services is being done at the local level. The second result was development of a Handbook on how to prepare local waste management plan, including all relevant EU and national legislation. Experiences from the process of drafting waste management plans throughout MSP Cajetina, Leskovac and Golubac were valuable input as they were organized through broad consultations and participation of all stakeholders (citizens, CSOs, business communities). The Handbook is shared with all LSGs and is expected to be used as a tool when preparing local waste management plans.
The direct efforts to work with gender mainstreaming and gender equality have also borne fruit. The gender MSPs have built institutional capacity in targeted LSGs to address their legal obligation to develop gender-responsive budgets and local action plans, which has generated models applicable for the broader membership of SCTM. More importantly, these efforts have resulted in an improved consciousness concerning public expenditure manifested by gender-conscious groups pushing for more resources being allocated to urban safety, health, childcare and recreation in order to achieve better local gender mainstreaming.
When the project started, the LSGs lacked capacity and procedures to develop a local business friendly environment. Existing practices were complicated, costly and time consuming. The financial capacities of LSGs were also identified as weak and they had few financing alternatives and mechanisms.
One key result of the project is that LSGs have realized the importance and benefits of broad co-operation at local level which has led to improved collaborations both between LSGs and with civil society/business environment. This has concretely led to LSGs now venturing into, for example, PPPs. Another concrete result is that business councils have been established in several LSGs, that now take a more comprehensive approach to local economic development (LED), including regular involvement of the business community in decision making processes for issues directly affecting company conditions such as for local employment plans and physical project plans. The work with value chain analyses has also broadened the local perception of sectors that can be competitive and why, which gives room for new sectors and businesses to grow.
Positive side effects of the project have also been a wider understanding of the importance of environmental protection and sustainability as a value for the local community. This perspective has also enhanced the level of innovation and readiness to strategically adapt the local environment to the expectations of the future in terms of green energy, ICT, ecological farming etc.
The LED unit at SCTM has also developed its capacity substantially during the project period, which has raised its credibility both among LSGs and the central actors, in turn resulting in higher recognition also at national level in Serbia. Through this unit, SCTM has become a member of different national working groups, for example the Working group for drafting the national Law on register of administrative procedures (for businesses and citizens) and the working group for Public Administration Reform Strategy. The knowledge and expertise gained in the LED MSPs have also led to proposed changes in the law for PPP as well as addressed the problem of economic data at local level to the ministries of economy, local government, trade, agriculture etc.
In very concrete terms, the standardization of administrative procedures proposed by SCTM LED unit led to the implementation of new procedures at local level, which has led to direct savings of an estimated three million EURO for citizens and businesses.
Within component for emergency management and disaster risk reduction (DRR) SCTM has built internal expertise and capacities in a field of general importance for all LSGs in Serbia. The changes that have been made since 2016 serve as a tool to improve the DRR system and to make local self-governments more resilient. Experience exchange and knowledge transfer among LSGs have helped the national authority, Sector of Emergency, to make important improvements to the national legal framework, for example, to make activities more transparent and include all groups of citizens in the prevention and planning of DRR, with a gender and human rights perspective.
In general terms, the project has successfully contributed to the overall objective: By 2022, Serbian municipalities will be better prepared for EU accession, with improved service delivery, enhanced dialogue with stakeholders and more efficient and transparent local administrations, by the principles of good governance and gender equality. All activities and expected short-term and medium-term outcomes of the project have been achieved during the project period contributing to envisaged long-term outcomes/results. This development is manifested in by-laws being adapted and regulations changed to respond to the needs of the LSGs. The new Gender Equality Law stipulated the presence of a Gender officer in each LSG. The gender MSPs have built institutional capacity in targeted LSGs to address their legal obligation to develop gender-responsive budgets and local action plans, which has generated models applicable for the broader membership of SCTM. More importantly, these efforts have resulted in an improved consciousness concerning public expenditure manifested by gender-conscious groups pushing for more resources being allocated to for example, urban safety, health, childcare, and recreation to achieve better local gender mainstreaming. The proactive measures of SCTM to conduct research and analyses concerning how different EU chapters may affect Serbian LSGs have earned recognition and respect both from the Serbian government and the local level. A majority of LSGs are now more aware of needed adjustments to become aligned with the EU-legal framework. By the end of the project, the EU dimension was observed and included in all project components as a cross-cutting theme.
